$comment: Generated by scripts/generate-sdk-contract.py. Do not edit. Every field is read from the Python implementation the conformance suite certifies; see that script's docstring.

precedence: explicit argument passed to the SDK constructor

settings.description: Chain id bound into EIP-712 domains. A signature is only valid for the chain it was signed against, so a mismatch here rejects every mandate with an unhelpful error.
settings.name: CHAIN_ID

settings.description: EVM RPC endpoint. Unset means in-memory verification.
settings.name: CHAIN_RPC

settings.description: Deployment key. Read from the environment and never written anywhere.
settings.name: DEPLOYER_KEY

settings.description: GitHub token for catalog harvesting and contract artifacts. Never needed by a running node.
settings.name: GH_TOKEN

settings.description: Alias for GH_TOKEN, checked second. Present because CI runners set this name by convention; a running node never needs either.
settings.name: GITHUB_TOKEN

settings.description: Disable ANSI colour in CLI output. Honours the no-color.org convention, so setting it to any value suppresses escape codes — useful when piping triage output into an incident ticket.
settings.name: NO_COLOR

settings.description: Collector endpoint. Enabled with no endpoint sends spans to the console, which is work nobody collects.
settings.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT

settings.description: Service name on exported telemetry.
settings.name: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME

settings.description: Refuse calls that did not arrive through a gateway. Setting 0 lets anyone reach the tools directly, bypassing every control.
settings.name: REQUIRE_VERIFIED

settings.description: RPC endpoint for contract deployment.
settings.name: RPC_URL

settings.description: Deployed SessionRegistry address. Required with CHAIN_RPC.
settings.name: SESSION_REGISTRY

settings.description: Path to an ABI override. Defaults to the generated artifact.
settings.name: SESSION_REGISTRY_ABI

settings.description: Path to solc for contract compilation.
settings.name: SOLC

settings.description: Fallback upstream credential when no vault backend is configured. Prefer a vault:// reference.
settings.name: UPSTREAM_CREDENTIAL

settings.description: Accept delegated tasks from peer gateways at /v1/a2a/accept. OFF by default: a node that accepts them is executing work on another datacentre's say-so, which an operator should decide deliberately rather than inherit from an upgrade. A ticket is still only admitted from a verified peer, in this node's cluster, naming this node, within its expiry, for the exact task committed to.
settings.name: XCP_A2A_ACCEPT

settings.description: How many boundaries one delegation may cross. Matches the federation's transitive-trust cap, for the same reason: beyond it nobody in the chain can reason about what they are part of. The originator sets the budget in the ticket and no hop can raise it.
settings.name: XCP_A2A_MAX_HOPS

settings.description: The most authority a cross-boundary delegation may carry HERE, whatever the originating gateway asserted. The asserted tier is narrowed leg by leg against this, so authority can only shrink at a boundary. The default is the top of the lattice, meaning 'whatever the origin verified'; an operator who wants delegated work capped lower sets e.g. A1xH1. The gateway refuses to start on a value it cannot parse, because a ceiling nobody can read is a ceiling that does not apply.
settings.name: XCP_A2A_TIER_CEILING

settings.description: Bearer token for /admin/* and the full peer list. When unset the administrative endpoints are DISABLED rather than open — an admin surface that defaults to open is worse than one that does not exist. Compared in constant time.
settings.name: XCP_ADMIN_TOKEN

settings.description: Permit peering over plain HTTP and to ANY private or loopback address. This disables the SSRF guard on the peer-record fetch and is for local development only; on a reachable node it lets a caller make the gateway fetch internal services. The production profile refuses to start with it set. For a private federation use XCP_PRIVATE_PEER_CIDRS, which is the scoped half of this and does not waive TLS.
settings.name: XCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_PEERS

settings.description: Seconds to cache a verification result. Longer means a revocation takes longer to bite.
settings.name: XCP_CACHE_TTL

settings.description: Address of the key allowed to sign this cluster's charters. Without it a node accepts any correctly-signed charter naming its cluster id, so anyone could mint one. Set it on every node.
settings.name: XCP_CLUSTER_AUTHORITY

settings.description: The cluster authority's signing key, read by scripts/cluster-charter.py. Belongs on the authority's machine only, never on a node: a node needs the address, not the key. UNRECOVERABLE if lost — every node is configured with the matching address and would need reconfiguring.
settings.name: XCP_CLUSTER_AUTHORITY_KEY

settings.description: Path to the signed cluster charter this node federates under. The charter commits to the member set with a Merkle root and carries no roster, so it can be distributed to every node without publishing who is in the cluster. A closed cluster refuses any peer whose membership proof does not verify against THIS charter's root — never against one the peer supplied. Unset means no cluster, and peering is bilateral. A charter that does not verify stops the node: starting without it would leave a closed cluster accepting any peer, which is what it exists to prevent.
settings.name: XCP_CLUSTER_CHARTER

settings.description: Path to THIS node's own membership proof, issued by the cluster authority. Published in the node record so peers can verify this node against their own charter. The node refuses to start if the proof does not verify, or if it is a proof for a different node — which catches a membership file copied from another datacentre.
settings.name: XCP_CLUSTER_MEMBERSHIP

settings.description: Refuse a charter below this epoch. Raising the epoch is how a member removal takes effect, so an operator pinning the floor stops a rolled-back charter file re-admitting a node that was removed. Set it to the epoch you currently expect.
settings.name: XCP_CLUSTER_MIN_EPOCH

settings.description: Identifier stamped on audit records and forwarded downstream as XCP-Verified-By.
settings.name: XCP_GATEWAY_ID

settings.description: Node-wide in-flight request cap.
settings.name: XCP_GLOBAL_CONCURRENCY

settings.description: Node-wide cost units per minute, independent of any caller's tier.
settings.name: XCP_GLOBAL_RATE

settings.description: Serve traffic if the limiter itself fails. Turns any limiter bug into an abuse bypass; only for private deployments behind another limiter.
settings.name: XCP_LIMIT_FAIL_OPEN

settings.description: Maximum bytes the gateway will relay in XCP-Upstream-Credential. The value is never read, logged or stored; this bounds what the pass-through will carry.
settings.name: XCP_MAX_UPSTREAM_CREDENTIAL

settings.description: keccak256(DER(cert)) of the certificate currently served. scripts/rotate-cert.py maintains this.
settings.name: XCP_NODE_CERT_FOOTPRINT

settings.description: Domain this node claims. Must match where the record is served.
settings.name: XCP_NODE_DOMAIN

settings.description: Long-lived node identity key. LOSING THIS IS UNRECOVERABLE: the node loses its identity and every attestation any peer made about it. Back it up offline before first use.
settings.name: XCP_NODE_KEY

settings.description: Operator name published in the node record.
settings.name: XCP_NODE_OPERATOR

settings.description: Serve the FULL node record to anyone, even in a closed cluster. A closed cluster gates its record by default — publishing the topology of a federation only members may join is incoherent, and gating also means a removed member loses discovery and not just peering. Set this for a node that must stay publicly discoverable: a public-facing gateway inside a private organisation, or one under external monitoring. It publishes this node's id, gateway URL, operator and seed peers.
settings.name: XCP_NODE_RECORD_PUBLIC

settings.description: This node's datacentre, region or zone — an opaque label you choose, e.g. 'dc1-dublin' or 'eu-west-1'. Peers prefer local routes over crossing a site boundary and apply their own residency rules against it. Unset means this node has no locality, so every peer is equally near and nothing is preferred. Published in the node record (a peer cannot observe it) and withheld from the reduced one.
settings.name: XCP_NODE_SITE

settings.description: Public gateway URL published to peers.
settings.name: XCP_NODE_URL

settings.description: Enable OpenTelemetry. Off by default; without it every instrumentation call is a no-op and the node behaves identically, so enabling it is a deliberate act rather than a default.
settings.name: XCP_OTEL

settings.description: scrubbed | hosts | full. `full` exports raw agent ids, scopes and hostnames — self-hosted collectors only. Sending it to a vendor is a new processor and usually an international transfer.
settings.name: XCP_OTEL_DETAIL

settings.description: PEM bundle of the certificate authorities that sign THIS federation's peers. When set it REPLACES the public trust store for peer-record fetches and certificate-footprint retrieval — and for those only, so upstream tool calls keep public trust. Needed for a private federation using an internal CA: chain validation ran against the system store and failed before the footprint binding was reached. A mixed deployment concatenates the public roots it needs into the same file, which keeps the trust decision in one auditable place. An unreadable or empty bundle stops the node starting; falling back to the public store would leave the operator believing peers are verified against their own CA.
settings.name: XCP_PEER_CA_BUNDLE

settings.description: Path to a policy document. When set, every governed call is evaluated against it and the gateway REFUSES TO START if the document cannot be loaded — a policy you asked for and did not get is a control you believe you have.
settings.name: XCP_POLICY

settings.description: Digest of the policy an auditor approved. The gateway compares it against the policy it is actually enforcing and warns on divergence, which is what gives the policy adjudicative standing rather than resting on the operator's word.
settings.name: XCP_POLICY_APPROVED_DIGEST

settings.description: enforce | observe. Observe logs decisions without blocking them — for onboarding an endpoint you have not vetted, never a steady state.
settings.name: XCP_POSTURE

settings.description: Comma-separated internal ranges that may hold federation peers, e.g. "10.40.0.0/16,fd00:dc1::/48". Without this a peer on a private address is unreachable, which made a private federation across datacentres impossible to run under the production profile. Narrower than XCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_PEERS in two ways: a host that resolves outside every declared range is still refused, and loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses stay refused even when a declaration contains them. TLS is still required. Declarations broader than /8 (IPv4) or /7 (IPv6) are refused as a disguised bypass, and a malformed entry stops the node starting rather than silently narrowing what you declared.
settings.name: XCP_PRIVATE_PEER_CIDRS

settings.description: development | production. The production profile refuses to start unless enforce posture, an external verifier, hardening, rate limiting, an admin token and secure peering are all in place — a profile that is claimed and not enforced is worse than one never claimed.
settings.name: XCP_PROFILE

settings.description: Abuse controls. Setting 0 on a node reachable by strangers makes it an open relay.
settings.name: XCP_RATE_LIMIT

settings.description: Comma-separated sites where a relayed tool call's data may be processed, e.g. 'eu-west-1,eu-central-1'. When set, a peer outside is INADMISSIBLE rather than merely expensive — a jurisdiction is not a quantity you can be compensated for crossing. A peer that declares no site fails this: not knowing where a peer is is not the same as it being somewhere permitted. Empty means no residency constraint.
settings.name: XCP_RESIDENCY_SITES

settings.description: Accept a throwaway sealing key. Every restart invalidates every sealed credential; local testing only.
settings.name: XCP_SEAL_EPHEMERAL

settings.description: Comma-separated previous sealing keys, accepted during a rotation so in-flight requests do not break.
settings.name: XCP_SEAL_PREVIOUS

settings.description: X25519 private key for sealed credentials. Without it a sealed wrapper refuses to start, because regenerating silently invalidates every credential already sealed to it.
settings.name: XCP_SEAL_PRIVATE

settings.description: Prefix for the env secret backend, e.g. XCP_SECRET_CONNECTORS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. Development only.
settings.name: XCP_SECRET_*

settings.description: Enable the xcpsec argument firewall. The gateway REFUSES TO START if this is 1 and xcpsec is unavailable, rather than running with a control you asked for silently absent.
settings.name: XCP_SECURITY

settings.description: Name this server answers to in XCP_UPSTREAMS.
settings.name: XCP_SERVER_NAME

settings.description: Ask a peer for a tool this node cannot reach. OFF by default: a call leaving for another datacentre is a different data path than the one configured in XCP_UPSTREAMS, and the operator should choose it. With it on, an unknown server is routed to a peer that advertises it, preferring the nearest site and refusing any site XCP_RESIDENCY_SITES does not permit.
settings.name: XCP_TOOL_FALLBACK

settings.description: Serve tool calls on a peer's behalf at /v1/tool/relay. OFF by default: relaying spends THIS node's vendor credential on another datacentre's say-so. A relayed call is admitted exactly as a cross-boundary delegation is — verified peer, this node's cluster, naming this node, within expiry, for the exact call committed to — and runs at the tier narrowed under this node's ceiling. Enabling it also advertises this node's upstream server names to peers.
settings.name: XCP_TOOL_RELAY

settings.description: JSON map of name to MCP url, e.g. {"research":"https://.../mcp"}. Empty means every a2t call 404s.
settings.name: XCP_UPSTREAMS

settings.description: The credential this node presents upstream when serving a relayed call. It belongs to THIS node — the asking datacentre never holds or sees it, which is the reason to centralise egress at all. Prefer a vault:// reference.
settings.name: XCP_UPSTREAM_RELAY_CREDENTIAL

settings.description: External verifier. Unset uses in-memory bindings, which is fine for one node and insufficient for a federation.
settings.name: XCP_VERIFY_URL

conformance.title: Opens a session and returns a binding
Refuses a call with no identity header
Refuses a call with no mandate
Refuses a scope the mandate does not cover
Accepts a valid session and mandate
The node record is well formed
Identity is not the certificate footprint
Does not require a session id header
Tolerates a legacy session id rather than failing

federation.localityRule: Locality is a cost: an off-site peer is priced at crossSiteCost and can still win. Residency is a constraint: a site outside permittedSites is inadmissible at any price.
federation.narrowingRule: Authority narrows at a boundary and never widens. The destination computes its own ceiling and takes the per-leg minimum; a ticket that would widen is refused, not clamped.

identity.footprintRule: Taken verbatim. Not lowercased, not 0X-normalised, not length-checked. It is compared byte-for-byte against a registered binding.
identity.integerRule: Fields 1 and 2 must be canonical decimal digits. Reject '+1', ' 1' and '1_0' even where the language's integer parser accepts them.
identity.name: xcp-agent-identity
identity.owsRule: RFC 9110 5.5: OWS = *( SP / HTAB ). Strip exactly these two characters from both ends. Do NOT use the host language's trim(): see sdk/vectors/identity_header.json for the eleven codepoints where they disagree.

reasons.nonCanonical: identity fields must be canonical decimal integers

lattice.ceilingRule: The ceiling is the weaker leg, resolved per leg with min(). A2xH0 is the one deliberate exception: a company-backed agent is not capped by an absent human, because the company is itself the principal.

cells.name: Sandbox
cells.notes: Read-only, rate-limited front door. No principal to bill or hold liable.

cells.name: Metered
cells.notes: Cheap writes against a personal cap; the verified human bears liability.

cells.name: Shadowed
cells.notes: Corporate human but unbacked agent: observe mode, audit-only, no settlement. Capped by the weaker leg — register the agent to unlock.

cells.name: Open marketplace
cells.notes: Reputation-bearing agent with no human principal — escrowed settlement only.

cells.name: Consumer commerce
cells.notes: Personal spend cap tied to a verified individual; marketplace counterparties.

cells.name: Delegated corporate
cells.notes: Budget and counterparties narrowed by entitlement attributes from the IdP.

cells.name: Service agent
cells.notes: Autonomous under the company's own liability — the company IS the principal. Deliberately NOT capped by the absent human.

cells.name: Professional
cells.notes: Company agent acting for one individual; contract-scoped.

cells.name: Full settlement
cells.notes: Enterprise ↔ enterprise. Entitlement-bound budget, all rails, complete audit. spend_cap 0 = no protocol cap; the entitlement supplies the real limit.

lattice.entitlementRule: Entitlements may only restrict the envelope.
